interventions.speaker: CHAIR
interventions.who: the senior urologist who signs the decision
interventions.body: Postoperative prognosis depends on the preoperative PSA and the prostatectomy findings. Extraprostatic extension is documented. Positive surgical margins is documented. Seminal vesicle invasion is reported absent. Lymphovascular invasion is reported absent. Postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory are needed to refine this prognosis; a future recurrence date cannot be established from surgical risk factors alone. The fixed estimated horizon is 32.85 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 24.63–41.06 months; its coverage has not been validated.

attempts.text: The postoperative pathology reveals a Gleason 4+3 with tertiary pattern 5 (ISUP grade group 3) and pathological stage pT3a. Adverse findings include positive surgical margins and extraprostatic extension. Countervailing findings include the absence of seminal vesicle invasion and lymphovascular invasion, and no lymph node metastasis were documented. Biopsy findings showed Gleason 3+4 (ISUP grade group 2). The absence of documented postoperative PSA means biochemical recurrence cannot be assessed. The pNx status does not establish node-negative disease, and missing nodal sampling widens uncertainty regarding regional disease control. Information regarding postoperative PSA and its trajectory is crucial for revising the prognosis. The documented negative findings regarding seminal vesicles and lymphovascular invasion offer some reassurance against local spread.

attempts.text: The postoperative pathology revealed a Gleason 4+3 with tertiary pattern 5 (ISUP grade group 3) and pathological stage pT3a. Extraprostatic extension was present, and surgical margins were positive. Countervailing findings include that the seminal vesicles were not invaded, and lymphovascular invasion was absent. The report also noted, "The robot-assisted radical prostatectomy specimen showed Gleason 4+3 with tertiary pattern 5 (ISUP grade group 3), pathological stage pT3a. Extraprostatic extension was present; surgical margins were positive; the seminal vesicles were not invaded; lymphovascular invasion was absent; there was no lymph node metastasis." Biopsy findings showed Gleason 3+4 in the peripheral zone with perineural invasion, but the histological growth pattern was described as "Acinar." The pNx status does not establish node-negative disease, and missing nodal sampling widens uncertainty regarding regional disease control. Postoperative PSA is not recorded, so biochemical recurrence cannot be assessed. Information regarding postoperative PSA and its trajectory would revise the prognosis.
